title: a-green-seal-crosses-the-boat-it-proves
author: CC
cast_under: Akien 2026-09-07: 'the 19 at proveme. what's the really, really right way to do this? spare no expense kind of thing?' -> CC's three pieces of physics -> 'then lets do that.'
intention: A green seal crosses the boat it proves: the tester tells codemother a proof sealed, codemother fires her cross verb for every ticket at PROVEME that names the proof, and the harbor door's PROVEME->PROVED gate admits only full coverage on a matching fingerprint, raising a trouble on refusal.
why: Measured 2026-09-07: 12 tickets sit at PROVEME:waiting with a green seal on the proof they name, some since 2026-09-04. Nobody fired the crossing because a crossing today is a mind remembering to run clearance.clear after a seal, and minds forget -- that is the whole 'waiting' pile. The operator's lived symptom: the inbox count says 19 waiting and the true number of boats needing a human is unknowable without opening each one. A decision with no judgment in it (green + covered + matching) should not wait for a person.
how: (a) `cairn test --seal` ends, per green seal, by sending codemother one `sealed` message over the bus (bus_client.connect_bus) carrying proof path, verdict, source_fingerprint and the validations path; a send failure is logged in the tester's log home and never blocks or unwinds the seal (the new measurement outranks the announcement -- same order as validation_store's verdict-change trouble). Sending is a tool; codemother owns what happens. (b) codemother's shim gains verb `sealed`: it scans CairnCommons/tickets for tickets at cursor PROVEME whose latest crossing proven_by is that proof and fires her own `cross <ticket-id> PROVED` (ticket 8754ae677af6) for each; concept-pieces never arrive here (a review VALIDATION is not a tester seal) and the handler says so. If she is down the message waits in the bus store and her next beat drains it (device-owns-its-subscription; the bus is a store, not a router). (c) clearance.clear's PROVEME->PROVED gate gains three rules, each hard and deterministic (ruling 2026-08-10 clearance-is-mandatory; Akien 2026-09-07: 'Gates are supposed to be hard, deterministic, state changes'): proof_covers_the_ticket (the sieve from ticket feeb4c786b14) returns no finding for this ticket; the seal's source_fingerprint matches the proof now; and for a code-seam the seal carries evidence.hollow[ticket] (ticket d0f2b03952e3) naming no hollow file -- absent hollow evidence is a red, the same as an absent seal. No rule has an advisory mode; a refusal raises a trouble through DiagnosticBase.raise_trouble (ticket 9579a6f9cec6) naming the ticket and the finding, so a hollow green becomes a live trouble instead of a parked boat. (d) The proof: a fixture bus + fixture tickets dir + fixture seal; one admission (journal cleared_by codemother) and one refusal (uncovered clause -> held trouble). DEPENDS ON: 8754ae677af6 (cross verb), proof-coverage sieve (P1), 9579a6f9cec6 (raise). Build order: (c) first -- the gate before the automation, never after.
falsifier: DONE when: (1) `cairn test --seal <fixture proof>` green produces exactly one `sealed` message in a fixture bus carrying proof path, verdict, source_fingerprint, validations path; (2) codemother's `sealed` handler, given a fixture ticket at PROVEME naming that proof with full coverage, produces a journal crossing to PROVED with cleared_by codemother; (3) the harbor door refuses PROVEME->PROVED for a fixture whose coverage finding is non-empty, for one whose seal fingerprint mismatches, and for a code-seam whose seal carries no evidence.hollow[ticket] or names a hollow file, and each refusal is one held trouble in a fixture store naming ticket and finding; (4) with no codemother process, a seal still lands green and the message is drained by her next `beat` -- no seal lost, no crossing faked; (5) a seal on a proof no PROVEME ticket names produces no crossing and no trouble. WRONG INTENT if a boat auto-crossed to PROVED is later redded by Akien for a reason a clause could have said: that is a falsifier gap in that ticket, fixed by a clause, never by a hand crossing or a switch on this path.
traces_to: Law 1 -- re-deriving 'is this proven?' by hand after every seal is the resolver spent on the settled. Law 6 -- codemother owns the care of the code, so the crossing carries her name (8754ae677af6's why); the tester only sends. Law 7 -- a refusal is a trouble, loud and permanent, not a log line. Law 8 -- the gate runs BEFORE the automation. Memory device-owns-its-subscription: message processing is command processing.
owner: codemother (cairn/devices/codemother) owns the sealed handler and the crossing; cairn's harbor_master owns the gate rule it adds; the tester's send is a tool call; CC builds
watchme: none, because every auto-crossing is a journal record with cleared_by codemother (cairn/devices/*/history.json, grep '"cleared_by": "codemother"') and every refusal is a held trouble in CairnCommons/troubles/ -- both counts are readable without a probe
children: none, because its three dependencies are already cast and at BUILDME: 8754ae677af6 (cross verb), 9579a6f9cec6 (inherited raise), and proof-coverage-is-declared-... (the predicate) cast in the same act

amended.why_verbatim: Akien: Gates are supposed to be hard, deterministic, state changes. no hollow evidence. that sounds like a bug.
amended.what: how (c) + falsifier (3): the hollow-evidence rule is the gate's third hard rule; absent evidence reds

phase_writes.why: its intention says the tester tells codemother and CODEMOTHER FIRES HER CROSS VERB — that verb is what 8754ae677af6 builds. The crossing cannot be admitted by a verb that does not answer yet.

8754ae677af6 reached PROVED (2026-09-09); the queue's reason is spent. Cleared to waiting rather than straight to a hand, so 'the dependency cleared' and 'a hand is on it' stay two recorded acts (the caster's read, recorded at /sorted and still unruled).
